newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan insurers plan to launch new products - paper.
newsitem.headline: Japan insurers plan to launch new products - paper.

text.p: Japanese insurance companies are planning to introduce new products this autumn, following an insurance agreement between Japan and the United States late last year, a Japanese business daily said on Wednesday.
The Nihon Keizai Shimbun said Japanese non-life insurance companies were planning to start mail-order sales of auto insurance and that life insurers were planning to offer medical coverage policies.
Japanese insurers were not immediately available for comment on the report.
In December, Tokyo and Washington reached an agreement that would open up Japan's $400 billion insurance market to greater international competition.
The deal aims at deregulating Japan's primary life, property and casualty insurance markets, in which foreign firms have a negligible share.
